title: Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Ensuring Integrity No. 2) Bill 2019
short_title: Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Ensuring Integrity No. 2) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill aims to strengthen rules for unions and employer groups after a royal commission found widespread misconduct.
It would let a court disqualify officers and cancel an organisation's registration for serious or repeated law-breaking, and require a public interest test for some mergers.
A new automatic disqualification would apply to anyone convicted of a criminal offence carrying a prison term of five years or more.
changes: Creates a new category of prescribed offence for automatic disqualification from office.
Gives the Federal Court power to disqualify officers on application by the Registered Organisations Commissioner.
Allows the Federal Court to cancel an organisation's registration on several grounds.
Expands the grounds for court-ordered remedial action, including appointing an administrator.
Requires the Fair Work Commission to apply a public interest test to amalgamations based on compliance history.
Directs the minister to commission an independent review of the amendments after two years.
summary.affected: Registered employee and employer organisations and their officers.

divisions.question: Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Ensuring Integrity No. 2) Bill 2019 - Second Reading - Put the question
The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2019-12-04.5.1) *that the resumption of the debate be made an order of the day for the next sitting.*

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: The government was accused of preventing debate on the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Ensuring Integrity No.2) Bill 2019, with the Prime Minister condemned for anti-democratic behaviour, petulance, and contempt for democracy.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: The opposition moved to suspend standing orders to debate the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Ensuring Integrity No.2) Bill 2019, arguing the government's attempt to prevent debate was anti-democratic and condemning the Prime Minister for petulance and contempt for democracy.
